title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/10/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Shortness of breath and productive cough.

Review of Systems:
The patient reports productive cough, fever, and generalized malaise. She denies chest pain, palpitations, or lower extremity edema. She denies any history of recent travel or known exposure to contagious illnesses.

Social History:
The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is a retired teacher and enjoys gardening. She denies any tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History:
Her mother had hypertension. Her father had a history of early-onset stroke.

Vitals:
Temperature: 101.4 F, Heart Rate: 88 bpm, Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg, Respiratory Rate: 20 breaths/min, SpO2: 94% on room air.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 13.5 x 10^9/L, Hemoglobin: 12.2 g/dL, Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L, Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL, eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2. Sputum culture: Negative. Blood cultures: Negative.

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 79-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with symptoms of pneumonia. Upon admission, she was febrile and reported significant fatigue. She was started on intravenous antibiotics and monitored for clinical improvement. Laboratory evaluation and sputum cultures were performed; however, no specific organism was identified, and all cultures remained negative. The patient showed a positive response to the antibiotic therapy, with a gradual decrease in temperature and improvement in oxygen saturation. She tolerated her diet well and was eventually deemed stable for transition to outpatient care.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Community-acquired pneumonia.

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin 500mg every 8 hours for 7 days.
Acetaminophen 650mg as needed for fever or discomfort.

Follow-up:
The patient is instructed to follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a reassessment of her respiratory status and to monitor for any recurrence of symptoms.

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, MD, 05/15/2026
explanations: Pneumonia with no organism identified: J18.9 (no HCC).
